title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python named 'Tippy' was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester and is now with Boston Animal Care and Control.
Residents reported someone abandoning the snake in a community garden, prompting a response from Animal Care and Control.
The python is in good condition at the city's animal facility in Roslindale; inquiries can be made at 617-635-1800.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Team Blue, led by Tommy DeVito, defeated Team White 22-15 in the Patriots' intra-squad scrimmage.
DeMario Douglas impressed for Team Blue, catching six passes including two touchdowns in the scrimmage.
Injury updates revealed Will Campbell will return after the weekend, while Carlton Davis is out until next week.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich was voted the best town on Cape Cod by over 850 Boston.com readers in an informal poll.
Harwich offers nearly 11 miles of tidal shoreline, seven villages, and more than 20 beaches along Nantucket Sound and Pleasant Bay.
The town is noted for its cultural activities, conservation areas, community centers, and a vibrant downtown area.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: The DA's office clarified that 'shut it off' was said about autopsy photos, not 'shut her up' as alleged.
Lindsay Clancy's attorney accused prosecutors of inappropriate comments, prompting a courtroom warning from Judge Sullivan.
The DA initially attributed the comment to its prosecutors, later stating it referred to taking down images of autopsy photos.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: 4-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu went viral for dancing at a DJ popup on Boston Common.
His mother, Chidimma Ikesinachi, captured and shared the video, which garnered over 200,000 likes.
Local DJ Miss S. Peace hosted the event, aimed at fostering human connection, where Chukwuemeka danced.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar in Boston will serve nonalcoholic porrón pours after three-day liquor license suspension.
The license was suspended after serving alcohol to seven underage patrons during a May inspection.
To prevent future incidents, the restaurant updated its ID policy and ordered more scanners.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots' wide receiver room includes seven potential candidates for roster spots, including A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs.
Coach Mike Vrabel is open to carrying seven wide receivers if it benefits the team's performance and roles.
Kayshon Boutte and Kyle Williams face uncertainties with trade rumors and competition for key roles in the offense.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates clashed over ethics and transparency in a Roxbury debate, with incumbent Kevin Hayden facing challenges from Rachael Rollins and Linda Champion.
Rollins criticized Hayden for inadequate gun violence response, while Champion emphasized the need for transparent police misconduct investigations.
Each candidate highlighted their experience: Hayden as incumbent, Rollins as former DA and U.S. attorney, Champion as a former prosecutor and community advocate.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat Advisory remains in effect as temperatures near 90°F with humidity making it feel close to 100°F.
The National Weather Service predicts potential pop-up showers and storms this Friday and Saturday evenings.
Humidity levels remain high this weekend, with a slight drop expected late Sunday into Monday.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Red Sox fan Andy Zides gifted Aroldis Chapman a vintage Bob Feller model glove from the 1930s during a game.
Chapman received the glove while watching the game from the bullpen and later allowed two earned runs after a month-long streak.
Despite Chapman's setback, the Red Sox won 12-11 in 13 innings against the White Sox at Fenway Park.
